Name: Siege of Saguntum and Outbreak of War
RagShortTexts: In 219 BC, Hannibal captured Saguntum south of the Ebro after eight months of siege,...

Variants.Content: In 219 BC, Hannibal Barca laid siege to the Iberian fortress of Saguntum, a Roman ally south of the Ebro River. Despite desperate appeals to the Roman Senate, no relief legions arrived. After an eight-month siege marked by fierce sapping and famine, the city fell. Surviving Saguntines cast their treasures and themselves into funeral pyres rather than submit. In Rome, Consul Fabius Buteo offered Carthage peace or war; the Suffetes chose war, igniting the Second Punic War.

Eight brutal months digging trenches under scorching Iberian sun! When their stone ramparts finally collapsed, those stubborn Saguntines burned their own gold and jumped into the flames before our blades could touch them!

Saguntum was the catalyst of destiny. Hannibal knew well that striking this Roman client would force the Republic's hand, dismantling the fragile Ebro compromise and launching the grand march upon Italy.
